claude_take: What strikes me about today's set is the gap between infrastructure and appetite. Nvidia and Google are racing to switch on their next generation of AI chips while a clear majority of Americans say AI is bad for society and don't want a data center anywhere near them; the buildout isn't waiting for permission. Hollywood's incentive math tells a similar story: California already throws money at production and it keeps leaving anyway, which is exactly why the industry is now asking Washington for a bigger, blunter version of the same tool. Even Hermès, the one luxury house that was supposed to be insulated from China's pullback, just posted its slowest growth since 2020, a reminder that nothing stays immune to a slowdown this broad forever.
claude_take_title: The Buildout Isn't Waiting for Permission

items.headline: Canva Launches Craft, Its First In-House AI Image Model
items.summary: Canva released Craft on October 22, its first text-to-image model built entirely in-house rather than licensed from a partner such as Leonardo.ai or Google. The model generates images up to 2K resolution, is available now to Canva users, and can be accessed by developers through a public API; it debuted in fourth place on DesignArena, a public leaderboard where people vote on AI-generated images. The move is a step toward Canva owning more of its own creative AI stack instead of depending on outside model vendors for the feature most central to its product.

items.headline: Google Cloud Brings Nvidia's Next-Generation Vera Rubin Chips Online
items.summary: Google Cloud put its first Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72-based A5X instances into early access this week at Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, with general availability planned for November and expansion into Europe to follow. Nvidia says the new systems deliver up to 10x lower inference cost per token and 10x higher token throughput per megawatt than the prior generation, vendor claims that have not been independently verified. The rollout underscores how aggressively cloud providers are racing to secure next-generation AI compute capacity.

items.headline: Hollywood Coalition Formally Backs Federal Film Tax Incentive
items.summary: A coalition of talent agencies and independent producers has thrown its weight behind the bipartisan federal film and TV tax incentive bill introduced in Congress, calling it a "first step" toward restoring US production levels. A Motion Picture Association-commissioned study estimates that a 20% federal credit could bring $125 billion in additional production spending to the US between 2027 and 2035, as runaway production continues to erode Hollywood's domestic base.

items.headline: California Film Production Keeps Falling Despite State Incentives
items.summary: A new FilmLA report shows on-location production in the Los Angeles area fell another 3.7% in the third quarter, even after California expanded its tax-credit program specifically to stem the exodus of shoots to other states and countries. The continued decline is a sobering data point suggesting state incentives alone have not reversed the slide, strengthening the case industry groups are now making for a federal-level fix.

items.headline: Supreme Court Rulings Reshape the Midterm Election Battlefield
items.summary: A string of Supreme Court decisions this year, loosening limits on coordinated campaign spending, curbing Voting Rights Act-based redistricting claims, and this week clearing New Hampshire to bar student IDs as valid voter ID, has systematically favored Republicans heading into next month's midterms. Justice Elena Kagan has publicly criticized the pattern, saying the court has "blinded itself to the very deleterious effect of their rulings on how the political system works."

items.headline: Most Americans Now Say AI Is Bad for Society, Poll Finds
items.summary: A new ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll, fielded October 9-13 and released October 21, finds 57% of Americans say AI is bad for society versus 42% who say it's good, with 66% opposed to new data centers nationally and even higher opposition when asked about one in their own community. The skepticism cuts across party lines, with majorities of Democrats and independents and roughly half of Republicans sharing the negative view, even as Americans are evenly split on whether AI is good for them personally.

items.headline: Hermès Growth Slows to Its Weakest Pace Since 2020 as China Stalls
items.summary: Hermès reported third-quarter sales growth of roughly 4%, its slowest pace since 2020, as the Asia-Pacific region that includes China stayed essentially flat against analyst expectations of modest growth, with Japan the one bright spot in the region. Hermès had been the luxury sector's rare holdout through China's downturn, so even a modest slowdown there is a signal of how deep and durable the region's pullback in high-end spending has become for the industry as a whole.

items.headline: Descartes's Cogito Ergo Sum
items.headline_fr: Le cogito ergo sum de Descartes
items.summary: In the Meditations, René Descartes set out to doubt everything he possibly could, his senses, his body, even the external world, searching for one truth immune to doubt. He found it in the act of doubting itself: even if he is being deceived about everything else, the fact that he is thinking proves he exists. "I think, therefore I am" became the foundation stone of modern philosophy's turn toward the thinking subject as the starting point for knowledge, a move that still shapes how we treat consciousness and self-certainty as the ground everything else must be built on.
items.summary_fr: Dans les Méditations, René Descartes entreprend de douter de tout ce qui peut l'être, ses sens, son corps, le monde extérieur lui-même, à la recherche d'une vérité qui résiste à ce doute radical. Il la trouve dans l'acte même de douter : même trompé sur tout le reste, le fait de penser prouve qu'il existe. « Je pense, donc je suis » devient le socle de la philosophie moderne, qui place désormais le sujet pensant au point de départ de toute connaissance, un geste qui continue d'informer la manière dont nous pensons la conscience et la certitude de soi comme fondations premières.
